parsed.main_gap: none (argument is complete once Q is read as the set of all primes ≤ A, as the proof itself consistently uses)

errors.description: Q is defined as the primes dividing A, but the whole Lemma argument ("all prime factors of x are at most A ⇒ σ(x)=P(x)", "primes in P(x)\σ(x) are greater than A") and the final L only work with Q = {all primes ≤ A}. With the literal definition the Lemma is false (A=15: 18 is a term, σ(18)={3} is not good since gcd(3,20)=1) and (4) fails (18 term, 33 not). The author's own discussion (hypothesis 1) confirms the intended Q is primes ≤ A, so this is a misstatement, but the accompanying sentence 'Only the primes dividing A can matter here' reinforces the wrong definition.

parsed.notes: Correct and elegant route: characterization (1) of terms via 'good' prime supports, the key lemma that the ≤A-prime trace of any term is already good (proved by a clean induction using the auxiliary term Rp^k), then translation invariance by L=∏_{p≤A}p on [A,∞) gives a_{n+T}=a_n+L for all n≥1. One point deducted for the inconsistent definition of Q.
